title: Binary Tree Right Side View
prompt:
Imagine standing to the right of a binary tree. Return the values of the nodes you can see, ordered from top to bottom.

**Example**: `[1,2,3,null,5,null,4]` → `[1,3,4]`.

**Constraints**: 0 ≤ nodes ≤ 100.

tests.note: deepest-right comes from the left subtree

hints: At each depth, exactly one node is visible from the right. Which one is it?
Go level by level (BFS with a frozen `size`). The visible node is the last one on each level. It isn't necessarily a right child.
Inside the level loop: `if (i == size - 1) res.add(node.val);`. Still offer both children, left before right, so the last node polled really is the rightmost.

solution.explanation: Children are offered left to right, so the last node polled on each level is the rightmost node at that depth, the one you see from the right. The `[1,2,3,4]` test shows that node can come from the left subtree. A DFS alternative visits right children first and records a node when `depth == res.size()`. O(n) time, O(w) queue space.
